title: I couldn't find an MMORPG I wanted to play, so I started making one... things got a little out of hand
author: foxql
selftext:
Hey guys,

I couldn't find anything I really felt like playing, so out of boredom I thought, **"screw it, I'll make an MMORPG myself."**

Well... things got a little out of hand.

What I'm trying to build is a much more casual kind of MMO. Something I can play for five minutes while I'm on the road, kill a couple of monsters while sitting on the toilet, then close it and get back to my life.

I don't want an MMO that feels like a full-time job where you have to be online 24/7 just to keep up.

The entire online infrastructure is already up and running. For the visuals, I went with the old-school **billboard sprite**technique used in retro games, and I feel like it accidentally gave the game a pretty unique/weird charm of its own.

You can also set up your own shop and trade with other players, kind of like **Metin2 or Silkroad**. So there's trading, exploration and combat all mixed together.

At this point I'm seriously considering finishing it and releasing it on mobile.

**Would you actually play something like this? Should I finish it?**

replies.author: foxql
replies.body: Yeah, fair point actually 😄 I was just getting pretty tired of all the pay-to-win stuff and MMOs that turn into a full-time job because of the endless grind. That's basically where the idea came from.

comments.author: game_plaza
comments.body: Something about the environment looks surreal and I'm digging it.

replies.author: foxql
replies.body: I actually want it to feel a little weird and surreal. The app stores are insanely competitive, so I'm hoping that weirdness might help it stand out a bit.

comments.author: elpsychris
comments.body: In psychology, the idea you are implementing is not new (check Idle RPG or incremental games). So I would check their subs and learn development and monetization tips from the experienced devs. As a dev and software engineer myself, I see no point in playing those games, but I love the idea of making one and learning the game-making art.
